mcqs.q: Examples of mobile technology include:
mcqs.explain: Mobile technology includes PDAs and smartphones — a logical transitional step from the personal computer.

mcqs.q: The MAIN motivation for HCPs adopting mobile devices is:
opts: Better communication and information resources at the point of care
mcqs.explain: A major driver is the need for better communication and information resources at the point of care.

mcqs.q: Which is a hospital information system (HIS) resource HCPs access on mobile?
mcqs.explain: HIS resources include EHRs, EMRs, clinical decision support systems (CDSS), picture archiving (PACS) and laboratory information systems (LIS).

mcqs.q: The MOST frequently used mobile medical program is:
mcqs.explain: Multiple studies show a drug reference is the most frequently used program, with personal scheduling second.

mcqs.q: Basic organizer functions on a smartphone include:
opts: Contacts, calendars, memos, tasks and password storage
mcqs.explain: All smartphones have organizer functions such as contacts, calendars and the ability to record memos, tasks and store passwords.

mcqs.q: With the evolution to cloud computing, medical programs are increasingly:
opts: Hosted on the cloud rather than on the device
mcqs.explain: With cloud computing, more and more medical programs are hosted on the cloud and not on the device.

mcqs.q: An 'app' is best defined as:
opts: A software program developed to run on a device for a specific purpose
mcqs.explain: Apps are software programs developed to run on a computer or mobile device to accomplish a specific purpose.

mcqs.q: Some advanced medical apps can even:
opts: Simulate surgical procedures or conduct hearing/vision tests
mcqs.explain: There are mobile apps that simulate surgical procedures or conduct simple medical exams such as hearing or vision tests.

mcqs.q: Apple's dedicated section for clinical apps is called:
mcqs.explain: Apple created the 'Apps for Healthcare Professionals' section within the medical category of the iTunes App Store; Google Play also offers HCP apps for Android.

mcqs.q: Epocrates, Skyscape and Medscape are examples of which app category?
mcqs.explain: Reference and information-gathering apps include Epocrates, Skyscape and Medscape; Lexi-Comp provides drug information.

mcqs.q: Lexi-Comp is a mobile app offering:
opts: Drug information references and decision-support tools (esp. for pharmacists)
mcqs.explain: Lexi-Comp offers a variety of drug information references and decision-support tools for the needs of pharmacists.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a medical CALCULATOR app?
mcqs.explain: Calculator apps include Cardiac Clearance (pre-surgery), Cholesterol (CHD risk), Depression and Growth Charts.

mcqs.q: Which is a smartphone OPERATING SYSTEM?
mcqs.explain: Smartphone operating systems include BlackBerry, Windows, iOS and Android.

mcqs.q: Which is a technology making mobile services a reality?
opts: GSM, SMS, WAP, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
mcqs.explain: Major enabling technologies include GSM, SMS, WAP, Bluetooth, WML and Wi-Fi (wireless fidelity).

mcqs.q: The Saudi app 'Tabaud' is designed to:
opts: Notify those in contact with people infected with coronavirus
mcqs.explain: Tabaud is a way to notify those who are in contact with people infected with coronavirus.

mcqs.q: 'Sehaty' is best described as:
opts: The Ministry of Health unified platform for health information and services
mcqs.explain: Sehaty is the unified platform of the Ministry of Health, giving users access to health information and several health services in Saudi Arabia.

mcqs.q: 'Tawakkalna' is described as a:
opts: Super-app unifying government services (aligned with Vision 2030)
mcqs.explain: Tawakkalna is the super app that unifies government services in one platform, in line with the goals of Vision 2030.

mcqs.q: Which is a LIMITATION of mobile technology?
opts: Slow inputting due to small keyboards/styluses
mcqs.explain: Limitations include slow inputting (small keyboards/styluses), small screens, security, expense (data plans) and adoption.

mcqs.q: Regarding mobile SECURITY in healthcare:
opts: Encryption and anti-viral programs are needed for patient-level data
mcqs.explain: As smartphones access enterprise/patient-level data, better security is needed; encryption and anti-viral programs for the mobile platform exist.

mcqs.q: Personal scheduling programs on smartphones commonly:
opts: Synchronize with Microsoft Outlook and Google
mcqs.explain: Personal scheduling is the second most-used function because most programs synchronize with Microsoft Outlook and Google.

mcqs.q: Medical textbooks on mobile devices are often:
opts: Purchased as apps (subscription) and updated annually, stored on SD cards
mcqs.explain: Many textbooks/journals are available as mobile apps after a subscription fee, are often updated annually, and can be stored on secure digital (SD) cards.

saqs.q: What resources do HCPs need to access at the point of care?
saqs.a: Communication (voice, video, text, email), hospital information systems (EHR, EMR, CDSS, PACS, LIS), informational resources (textbooks, guidelines, literature, drug references), and clinical software (diagnosis aids, calculators).

saqs.q: List the basic organizer functions of a smartphone.
saqs.a: Contacts, calendars, memos, tasks and password storage — allowing work calendars to be synchronized to the device.

saqs.q: List the purposes for which HCPs use mobile devices and apps.
saqs.a: Administration (information & time management), health-record maintenance/access, communication & consulting, reference & information gathering, clinical decision-making, patient monitoring, and medical education & training.

saqs.q: Give categories of medical apps for HCPs with examples.
saqs.a: Information management (Evernote), communication/consulting (Doximity), reference (Epocrates, Skyscape, Medscape), patient monitoring (Archimedes), education (QuantiaMD), and calculators (Cardiac Clearance, Growth Charts).

saqs.q: Name the Saudi medical apps and their purpose.
saqs.a: Tabaud — COVID contact notification. Sehaty — MoH unified platform for health info/services. Tawakkalna — super-app unifying government services (Vision 2030).
